title: Bind host TCP streams to negotiated Nostr sessions before desktop access
description: Static verified inherited security defect, found by md-70v.3 review (not caused by role adoption). src/host/main.c assigns ctx.client and sends initial UI tree immediately after accept (around 1254-1272); handle_client_packet MD_PKT_SESSION_INFO activates any parseable session acceptance without comparing negotiated ID (around 396-414), and input dispatch lacks per-connection granted-cap checks. Keep unproven streams inactive; validate/consume authorization once, bind proof to stream and gate video/tree/actions/input by granted capabilities. Add private deterministic unauthorized-second-client and wrong-session/capability tests. Outside md-70v.3 startup-only host scope.
notes: Implemented local-only commit bd8eefacf01d4b0360a60038196714f0c0fa6783 on fix/md-mrw-session-binding; not pushed/merged. Transitional v1 session_accept DM carries CSPRNG one-use 256-bit stream_token; first bounded SESSION_INFO must be exact session_bind with negotiated ID/token. Token-free authoritative ACK before capture publication; stream-owned VIDEO/AGENT/INPUT gates; extra clients and wrong/expired/replayed/duplicate proofs close. Acceptance moved after listener/backend readiness. Old tokenless clients and unauthenticated direct TCP fail closed; full P3.8 lifecycle explicitly deferred in docs/stream-binding.md. Final macOS meson suite27/27; all NIP46/NIP55L/NIP5F signers30/30; focused ASan2/2; host_binding217 checks with no skips; Linux full28/28 serial, compile-j2 with requested nostrc paths. Live desktop/a11y/input cases retain opt-in skips; no live GNOME access. Initial parallel Linux private bus fixture flake recorded as new md-dzm; isolated retry passed. Diff-scoped nostr-protocol-smells A-J found no newly introduced smells; Oracle review startup/deadline corrections applied. No nostr.* or allowlist-condition edits. VM ~/wt-mrw and all three task build dirs removed; no owned VM processes. Local evidence /tmp/md-mrw-evidence; VM /tmp/md-mrw-linux-testlog.*.

title: NIP-51 allowlist trusts relay filters and races the pool thread (F4/F6)
description: Slop audit docs/reviews/slop-audit-nostr.md F4, F6. F4: nostr.c:466-485 accepts any kind:30000 with d-tag metadesk-allowlist regardless of author and without signature check (pool->signature_checker is NULL) -> relay can inject an allowlist; compare pubkey to n->pk_hex and call nostr_event_validate(). F6: n->allowlist is written on the pool worker thread and read/mutated by md_nostr_is_allowed/add/remove/get_entry with no mutex, while dedup_mu guards the ring in the same struct; add allowlist_mu.
close_reason: F4/F6 fixed: author+signature check on kind:30000, allowlist_mu, copied get_entry.

title: Nostr publish path reports success it never observed (F1/F7/F9)
description: Slop audit docs/reviews/slop-audit-nostr.md findings F1, F7, F9. F1: md_nostr_send_dm hand-rolls NIP-17 and omits the ['p', recipient] tag that our own kind:1059 subscription filters on (#p), so DMs are undeliverable via compliant relays; use nostr_nip17_create_rumor/create_gift_wrap (dep_nip17 already linked). F7: nip55l_sign_event stamps sig onto an event with no id; use nostr_nip55l_sign_event_json(). F9: publish_all always returns 0; use nostr_relay_publish_and_wait().
close_reason: F1/F7/F9 fixed: nip17 builders adopted (p tag + randomized ts), nip55l_sign_event_json, publish_and_wait with all-reject failure.

title: Critical: Unauthenticated HTTP MCP endpoint with CORS wildcard
description: mcp_http.c POST /mcp and GET /mcp accept any request with no authn/authz, origin validation, CSRF protection, or per-client authorization. Since MCP tools trigger input actions on the host desktop, this is a remote code execution vector if bound beyond localhost. Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * is sent for all responses. max_clients config is declared but never used; hardcoded MAX_SSE_CLIENTS 4 controls capacity.
close_reason: fixed

title: Critical: PipeWire frame buffer leak and data race in on_process()
description: capture_pipewire.c:604-610 on_process() overwrites pending_frame/held_pw_buf if a previous frame is still unreleased. The old PipeWire buffer is never requeued, causing buffer starvation/leak and data lifetime races. Also pw_stop() does not signal frame_cond before join (line 814-826), blocking get_frame(). Init failure paths (710-726) leak partially-created core/stream/portal resources.
close_reason: Closed

title: Critical: Use-after-free in NIP-17 DM unwrap (nostr.c)
description: dm_unwrap_thread() keeps sender_pk as a pointer into seal, frees seal at line 398, then uses sender_pk at lines 406-408. Incoming NIP-17 DM handling dereferences freed memory. Fix: copy sender_pk before freeing seal.
close_reason: Fixed sender pubkey lifetime by copying before freeing seal; targeted Nostr test passes.

title: Wire session keepalive: host and client never detect a silent peer
description: Verified: src/core/session.c md_session_on_ping/on_pong/is_timed_out (keepalive_ms=5000, x3) have no production caller (tests/test_session.c only). Host src/host/main.c:2215 pings every 1s purely for RTT and never acts on missing traffic; client src/client/main.c:1500 treats recv timeout as 'keep waiting' forever. A peer that vanishes without RST (sleep, Wi-Fi drop, FIPS route loss) leaves the host holding the session and the client frozen on a stale frame, never reconnecting. Also md_session_on_ping/on_pong take uint32_t timestamps into uint64_t fields. Fix: seed on bind, refresh on every received packet, drop after keepalive*3 silence; regression via tests/direct_ip_session.py proxy blackhole.
close_reason: Merged to master (db21732, b33407d); regression tests fail before and pass after on macOS

title: stream: md_stream_recv discards a partially read packet on poll timeout (desync on slow links)
description: Found by md-ah9.6 (deploy/containers/reference/mesh-video-validation.md). md_stream_recv (src/core/stream.c) applies the caller's poll timeout as a deadline for the WHOLE packet: read_exact() returns 1 (timeout) after it has already consumed part of the header or payload, and md_stream_recv returns 1 with the stream still 'connected' and those bytes discarded. The next call parses mid-payload bytes as a header -> -1 -> 'client: connection lost'. Callers poll with tiny deadlines (client main loop 16 ms, host stream loop 10 ms), so any packet that takes longer than that to arrive desyncs the stream. On a LAN bridge a 1080p keyframe lands within 16 ms (md-ah9.11 passed); over a FIPS mesh (~5 Mbit/s on the VM) every session died after the first decoded frame (host 'client #1 disconnected (sent 5 frames)'), deterministically, while raw framed TCP over the same fips0 path verified byte-exact (824/978 messages, TCP_NODELAY on and off). Any slow WAN path is exposed. A VM-only scratch fix (deadline bounds only the wait for a packet's first byte; once started, finish the packet within 10 s, else disconnect) made all md-ah9.6 cells pass (133/133). The real fix should keep per-stream partial-read state (resumable header/payload) so short polls stay non-blocking, and cover TLS (ssl_io) as well.
acceptance_criteria: A packet whose bytes arrive across several recv polls is delivered intact (unit test: socketpair writer trickles a valid header+payload slower than the poll timeout); timeout before any byte still returns 1; md-ah9.6 validate-mesh-video.py passes on unpatched images.

title: nostrc: event-driven AUTH-OK recovery for protected pool subscriptions
description: Metadesk md-xcy dependency. Current libnostr/src/relay.c nostr_relay_auth calls nostr_relay_publish (EVENT, not AUTH), takes a signing callback without userdata, and has no AUTH-specific acknowledgement helper. AUTH envelope serialization + relay_write + per-relay OK callback let Metadesk sign off-reader and observe acceptance/rejection without editing nostrc. However simplepool.c pool_drain_all retires/frees CLOSED subscriptions, while pool_reconcile_subs blindly refires missing subscriptions on a <=200ms cadence, even before AUTH succeeds or after AUTH/restricted rejection. get_callback_subscription is borrowed only within middleware/state callback, not an owned event-driven retry handle. Need an AUTH-result-aware per-relay subscription pause/resume/retry API (or pool-owned AUTH bridge with userdata/cancellation) that reissues protected REQ exactly on successful current-generation AUTH OK, not timer polling, and leaves rejection closed until a new challenge/explicit action. Include private relay rejection/re-auth/CLOSED and reconnect tests. Do not modify nostrc sources in Metadesk work.
notes: 2026-11-18: user decided to lift Groundhog's GhRelayScope/GhRelayAuthSigner approach into libnostr under nostrc bead nostrc-7i6w (scope recorded there as design). md-1be is satisfied when nostrc-7i6w lands; metadesk then adopts the library API to close md-xcy.
close_reason: nostrc-7i6w merged into nostrc master cfcb86296: library-owned NIP-42 AUTH session + AUTH-OK-driven protected-REQ recovery. Metadesk adoption tracked by md-xcy.

title: Harden signer/bridge concurrency, DM auth, teardown (md-70v P2.6)

Implemented and committed locally: fc1d1f757a38aea072bbda4d88abc54bfa101ceb. No push or merge. Only src/core/nostr.c/.h, signer.c/.h, tests/test_nostr.c and test_signer.c changed; no host/client/MCP/Meson/nostrc source edits.

description: Make the MCP host safe to run unattended in a container. Plan: docs/plans/container-runtime-2026-11-14.md §1.1 W1, §7.0, §7.1, §7.4 Q4/Q5.

title: client: overlay+video use two separate SDL_RenderPresent calls -> ghost trails + mis-scaled video
description: on_decoded() calls md_renderer_present() (clear+copy video+present) while the main loop's render_client_overlay()->render_draw_data() does a second SDL_RenderPresent() after drawing ImGui, with no clear or video redraw. On a double-buffered SDL_Renderer the two present sources flip-book: moving the overlay leaves ghost trails of its prior positions, and the visible buffer alternates between a full video frame and a stale/half-scaled one (remote desktop appears shrunk to the top-left quarter on HiDPI). Fix: one render pass per frame — begin(clear+copy video at scale 1) -> draw overlay -> single present.
close_reason: Fixed and verified live: video fills window, single-present (no trails), restore_token skips consent, mouse/keyboard forwarded (remote cursor tracks + hover responds, host rx grows)

title: host: capture thread exits before PipeWire stream reaches STREAMING (frames=0, black screen)
description: capture_thread_func()'s loop guard is md_capture_is_active(), which is only true once on_state_changed sees PW_STREAM_STATE_STREAMING. host_wait_capture_dimensions() returns as soon as on_param_changed sets width/height (during format negotiation, before STREAMING), so the thread is spawned while active is still false and exits immediately — the stream delivers frames into pending_frame but nobody consumes them (host frames=0 sent=0, client black screen). Reproduced cross-host: Mac client ↔ Ubuntu 24.04 GNOME Wayland VM; link active, format BGRx 1512x909 negotiated, yet 0 frames. Native fast Linux usually wins the race. Fix: capture thread waits up to ~5s for active before its pull loop.
close_reason: Fixed in d358f1a; verified by live cross-host stream (Ubuntu VM host -> macOS client)

title: host: odd capture dimensions (e.g. 1512x909) make encoder creation fail
description: md_encoder_create() rejects odd width/height (NV12 needs even), and host/main.c passes the raw capture dimensions straight through, so a display with an odd edge — observed with a 1512x909 GNOME session in a UTM VM — aborts the host with 'failed to create encoder'. Fix: round encoder dims down to even; accept capture frames up to 1 px larger in the frame-size check (md_encoder_submit already crops via the caller stride); keep true display size for input injection.
close_reason: Fixed in d358f1a; verified by live cross-host stream (Ubuntu VM host -> macOS client)

title: host dies with SIGPIPE on Linux when a client disconnects mid-send
description: On Linux a client that closes immediately after connect (e.g. a port probe) makes the host's initial UI-tree send hit a closed socket; write() raises SIGPIPE and metadesk-host is killed (observed on Ubuntu 24.04 aarch64; ssh reported exit 255 = signal). macOS masks this via SO_NOSIGPIPE semantics. Fix: ignore SIGPIPE in host/client main (and/or use MSG_NOSIGNAL in stream.c sends) and treat EPIPE as connection lost.
close_reason: Fixed in d358f1a; verified by live cross-host stream (Ubuntu VM host -> macOS client)

title: capture_pipewire: SelectSources sends persist_mode as boolean; portal method errors ignored
description: portal_screencast_open() appends persist_mode as a D-Bus boolean, but org.freedesktop.portal.ScreenCast.SelectSources types it as 'u'. xdg-desktop-portal (1.18, Ubuntu 24.04) rejects the call with a method error and emits no Response, so portal_wait_response() times out after 5 s and capture silently falls back to a direct PipeWire connect with no screen stream. Also portal_wait_response() discards method-error replies, hiding the cause. Fix: send uint32 0; log and fail fast on DBUS_MESSAGE_TYPE_ERROR.
close_reason: Fixed in d358f1a; verified by live cross-host stream (Ubuntu VM host -> macOS client)

title: Linux build broken: strict c17 hides POSIX/GNU decls; uinput_destroy linkage mismatch
description: Building on Ubuntu 24.04 (gcc 13, aarch64) fails: (1) c_std=c17 sets __STRICT_ANSI__ so glibc hides struct addrinfo (stream.c, fips_addr.c), F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC (capture_pipewire.c) and ssize_t/locale_t needed by PipeWire's spa/utils/string.h — need _GNU_SOURCE project-wide on Linux; (2) input_uinput.c:336 'static declaration of uinput_destroy follows non-static declaration'. macOS builds fine because its headers are not strict. Found while bringing up metadesk-host on a UTM Linux VM.
close_reason: Fixed in d358f1a; verified by live cross-host stream (Ubuntu VM host -> macOS client)

Fix: add build-tree generated include dirs when present; accept either libgo archive name.

title: client: SDL event queue has two destructive consumers; double RenderPresent
description: Code: S7. Files: src/client/render.c:160,167 vs src/client/ui.cpp:110-112,600-602. Evidence: render.c SDL_PollEvent drains the queue before ImGui's SDL_PeepEvents(SDL_GETEVENT) runs, so F1 overlay toggle and the Disconnect button are effectively dead; both render.c and ui.cpp call SDL_RenderPresent, the overlay path presenting without clear/copy. Correct shape: single event pump feeding ImGui (ImGui_ImplSDL2_ProcessEvent) then app handling; single present at end of frame. Cost: dead UI controls, ordering fragility.
close_reason: Single pump: renderer forwards events to overlay via callback; overlay drain removed. (Double RenderPresent left as-is — second present carries overlay, harmless without vsync; noted.)

title: a11y: push events discarded, full desktop re-walk under the backend lock
description: atspi_change_event_cb (a11y_atspi.c:282), axui_observer_cb (a11y_axui.m:470) and UIAChangeHandler::emit_change (a11y_uia.cpp:602) all (void) the event payload and call get_diff_unlocked while holding the lock, re-walking the whole desktop over IPC. macOS subscribes kAXValueChanged, which fires per keystroke. Build deltas from the event (element/notification/changeType/runtimeId), coalesce with a debounce timer, never hold the lock across IPC. See docs/reviews/slop-audit-media.md finding A3.
acceptance_criteria: a single focus change does not trigger a full-desktop walk; no lock held across a cross-process call
notes: Audit re-verified 2026-09-21. Acceptance #2 (no lock held across cross-process call) is ALREADY satisfied in all three backends: atspi_change_event_cb, axui_observer_cb, and UIAChangeHandler::emit_change each capture cb under the lock, unlock, THEN call md_a11y_diff (see the 'Diff outside the backend lock' comments; landed with md-0uf/md-h82). Remaining = acceptance #1 only: each event still triggers a full-desktop md_a11y_diff. Correct fix is per-platform subtree deltas built from the event payload (AtspiEvent.source/type/detail1; AXUIElementRef+notification; IUIAutomationElement+runtimeId) plus a get_subtree backend seam and burst coalescing. This is genuinely platform-specific and only the macOS (AXUI) backend is buildable on the current darwin host; atspi (Linux) and uia (Windows) need per-OS CI to land safely. Deferring rather than shipping a blind, unverifiable threaded coalescer + 3-backend rewire (would violate the audit's 'no unverifiable complexity' rule). Keep P1.
close_reason: Merged to master as b530596 (d6c46e3, 0c612ad, 9c631c6, 9b65950). Acceptance #1 met platform-neutrally: backends dispatch a change HINT (md_a11y_change_dispatch) with no md_a11y_diff/get_tree per event; MCP consumer invalidates the lazy snapshot and emits one coalesced notifications/resources/updated per burst (50ms quiet / 200ms cap, bounded retry). Seed walks on subscribe removed. Verified: 22/22 unit, MCP suites x10 serial, ASan clean, live macOS 1 hint -> 0 get_tree. a11y_atspi.c syntax-checked; a11y_uia.cpp edit mechanical and UNCOMPILED (needs Windows build). Per-platform subtree deltas from event payload remain deferred — only needed for consumers wanting pushed content, none exist today.

title: a11y: node IDs are per-walk DFS counters, not stable identities

Inserting one node shifts every later ID so the tree tail reports as changed. Use atspi_accessible_get_path(), IUIAutomationElement::GetRuntimeId() (already delivered to HandleStructureChangedEvent and (void)'d at a11y_uia.cpp:588), and CFHash(AXUIElementRef)+pid. See docs/reviews/slop-audit-media.md finding A2.

close_reason: Stable IDs on all 3 backends (macOS verified, others reviewed blind).

title: a11y: hoist triplicated diff engine into a11y.c

The comment justifies this for KEY_COMBO/TYPE but the code continues for all types; region[] is zeroed, so a CLICK on a stale node ID injects a real click at screen (0,0) and reports success. title: mcp_http: no read timeout on accepted sockets; shutdown can hang

An idle connection parks a go() handler forever; md_mcp_http_shutdown closes only SSE fds, so md_mcp_http_destroy's go_wait_group_wait never returns. title: GNOME capture: don't issue portal Start while the session is locked; ack Request.Close before Session.Close
description:
md-8gzk reproduced the GNOME xdg-desktop-portal-gnome crash: when a pending ScreenCast.Start chooser is cancelled, 46.2 always crashes (two use-after-free paths, upstream 9a4dffa in 47.0 and 056029c in 50.0). On a locked GNOME session Mutter inhibits session creation, so restore always fails, the backend falls back to a chooser behind the lock screen, metadesk times out after 180 s, cancels, and the backend SEGVs. The frontend has already consumed the restore token, so remembered consent is lost too. No close ordering avoids the crash on 46.2 (10/10 runs crashed). On 47-49 (9a4dffa only) the Request.Close-then-Session.Close order survives but Session-first still crashes; the 1.18 frontend runs each method in a worker thread, so metadesk's back-to-back no-reply burst can arrive in either order. Full analysis: docs/reviews/md-8gzk-gnome-portal-cancel-crash.md.

Mitigation (line numbers at cb7b1cd; re-locate after md-kmoa lands, which owns these files now):
M1 lock gate in src/core/capture_pipewire.c portal_screencast_open (L283; before Step 1 CreateSession L324, or at the latest before Step 3 Start L428): if the session is locked (org.gnome.ScreenSaver.GetActive on the session bus, or logind Session.LockedHint for our own session), do not issue Start. Fail with a distinct 'desktop locked' capture error, or subscribe to ScreenSaver.ActiveChanged and proceed on false within the existing consent deadline (event-driven, no polling). Never Start-then-cancel.
M2 deterministic cancel: portal_wait_response L228-235 sends Request.Close no-reply, then portal_screencast_close L600-616 sends Session.Close (no-reply at L613-616 once the consent budget is spent, L607), then disconnects at L624. Instead send Request.Close with a reply and wait for it (or Response) within a small fixed cleanup budget independent of the consent deadline, then Session.Close and await its ack, then disconnect. Keep Request-before-Session; do NOT reorder to Session-first.
M3 apply both to the shared portal-session owner md-kmoa introduces (RemoteDesktop.Start did not crash in 4/4 runs on 46.2, but its handle_close/session-close lifetime is also unsound upstream).
Do not touch capture_pipewire.c/input_portal.c until md-kmoa merges.
acceptance_criteria: Private-session fixture: with a locked/inhibited GNOME (or fake ScreenSaver.GetActive=true), host capture start issues no ScreenCast/RemoteDesktop Start, reports a distinct locked status within the consent budget, and the persisted restore token survives. Unit-level check that cancel sends Request.Close, awaits its reply, then Session.Close. No live-desktop lock/unlock in tests.
notes:
Re-located after md-kmoa merged (master 8be1c74). Default interactive GNOME Wayland hosts now take the paired RemoteDesktop path: src/core/input_portal.c md_portal_session_create, Start at L628-629; cancel via close_object L152-164 = Request.Close with reply (1000 ms), then Session.Close acked in md_portal_session_unref L545, then disconnect L549. That already satisfies M2, and RemoteDesktop.Start did not crash on 46.2 in md-8gzk tests. The legacy ScreenCast path still runs for --no-input, --managed, --input-backend uinput|wayland, X11 sessions and builds without MD_HAVE_PORTAL_INPUT (src/host/main.c L1927-1941). There, src/core/capture_pipewire.c still sends no-reply Request.Close at L230-238, then Session.Close (no-reply once the budget is spent, L610/L617) and disconnects at L627; Start is at Step 3 L439-447. M1 (lock gate) applies to both: before input_portal.c L628 and before capture_pipewire.c Step 3 L439 (ideally before Step 1 L341 / CreateSession). M2 applies to the legacy path only.
Correction: in master's input_portal.c the session Close is at L548, not L545.
Private Ubuntu 24.04 aarch64 VM: new regressions failed on a5602b3 (8/563 capture and 23/479 portal/EIS assertions failed). Fixed source passed 563 capture and 479 portal/EIS checks in both normal and GCC ASan+UBSan runs (2 suites, 0 failed/skipped); ASan/UBSan run did not include leak detection. Separate LSan run found the same PipeWire export leak on unmodified a5602b3 and the patched fixture; see md-9aak. metadesk-host was compiled, never launched on VM. VM cleanup receipt 2026-11-24T05:57:40Z: collected private fixture/build jobs; /home/bizarro/md-xhkx absent, no task-root /proc cwd/executable or Unix socket references. No live desktop, consent UI, lock/unlock, service restart, uinput or AT-SPI was used. Owner-attended qualification remains NOT RUN; see docs/testing/input-portal.md, GNOME lock gate qualification.
2026-11-24 follow-up: Oracle review found the legacy ScreenCast path skipped Request.Close when a request METHOD reply was lost or late (e.g. a Start reply timing out), so Session.Close went first. Fixed in 9a84a69: a NoReply/TimedOut/Disconnected method failure now sends an awaited Request.Close on the predicted request path and skips Session.Close unless it is acked. An explicit error reply is still treated as a refusal. New test_capture mock mode 9 covers this. CI run 45338738409 on 9a84a69: macOS passed; Ubuntu was cancelled at the 25-minute job timeout in all 3 attempts while apt-get install was crawling on us-east-2.ec2.archive.ubuntu.com (infra; no build or test step ran). NOT merged: 9a84a69 is uncompiled on Linux. Next: rerun the Ubuntu job; once it is green, merge --no-ff into local master, delete the remote and local branch and the worktree, close md-xhkx, and add the md-8gzk note.

title: GNOME 46.2 portal backend crashes when an inhibited restore request times out
description: Dependency/environment defect observed during L7 with Ubuntu xdg-desktop-portal 1.18.4-1ubuntu2.24.04.3 and xdg-desktop-portal-gnome 46.2-0ubuntu1. Read-only checks show live GNOME LockedHint=yes and ScreenSaver.GetActive true. On restore, backend journal at Nov21 19:40:11 local says Error restoring stream from session: Session creation inhibited, confirming valid restore data reached the GNOME path. At19:43:10 the configured180s portal request times out; at19:43:12 GNOME portal backend exits code=dumped status11/SEGV. A later DBus activation at19:50:51 exposes no ScreenCast interface while still locked. L7 did not restart any service, unlock/lock the desktop, create uinput, or disturb AT-SPI. This is not evidence of a metadesk token replay/persistence bug; trace ownership/cancel race upstream in a disposable/private session.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce the lock/inhibited-restore/cancel path on an isolated desktop and determine/fix or upstream the portal crash; preserve consent and lock boundaries. Qualify normal restore only after a human unlock; no service-restart workaround on the shared desktop.
notes:
2026-11-23 investigation (report docs/reviews/md-8gzk-gnome-portal-cancel-crash.md). REPRODUCED deterministically in an isolated headless GNOME 46 session on the VM (private dbus-run-session/HOME/XDG_RUNTIME_DIR; mutter inhibit_remote_access via private-shell Eval, since headless shell skips lock inhibit; seeded private permission-store restore data; backend under gdb through private D-Bus activation). The faithful metadesk sequence (inhibited restore -> 'Session creation inhibited' -> chooser fallback -> timeout -> no-reply Request.Close + Session.Close + disconnect) SEGVs every time; 10/10 stock runs crashed, including with no restore/inhibit (pending chooser only). ROOT CAUSE, two lifetime bugs in 46.2 src/screencast.c: (A) on_request_handle_close_cb L210-217 frees ScreenCastDialogHandle without clearing session->dialog_handle, so screen_cast_session_close L916 frees it again (gtk_window_destroy/g_object_unref, or malloc abort); fixed by 9a4dffa (MR !164), in 47.0+, never released on 46.x (gnome-46 has 7c44035, no 46.3 tag). (B) session close frees the handle but leaves the Request handle-close handler connected, so a later Request.Close UAFs in cancel_start_session L203/L214 (same signature as the Nov 14 /var/crash core); fixed only by 056029c (MR !231), in 50.0+, gnome-49 backport untagged, not on 47/48. The 1.18.4 frontend forwards the two closes from worker threads, so either order can happen. A/B builds: 46.2+9a4dffa survives Request-first and disconnect but crashes Session-first; 46.2+both fixes survives all four. Upstream: GNOME #60 (open, Needs Information, same B stack); LP #2103434 (New, no noble task); noble ships 46.2-0ubuntu1 unfixed. RemoteDesktop.Start (master default after md-kmoa) did not crash on 46.2 in 4/4 orderings. metadesk: the timeout length is irrelevant; no close ordering is safe on 46.2; Session-first is harmful on 47-49. Mitigation filed as md-xhkx (lock gate before Start; ack Request.Close before Session.Close on the legacy path). Ready-to-file upstream comment/SRU text is in the report; NOT filed (owner decision). Cleanup: ~/md-8gzk removed, all private processes stopped, live session untouched. Apport briefly replaced the /var/crash xdpg report twice during early racy runs; the original Nov 14 report was restored (same size/mtime), and the live update-notifier may show a crash prompt after unlock. Leaving open: needs the upstream/SRU decision and fixed-backend qualification.
metadesk mitigation landed in 1e78537 (md-xhkx); upstream fix still pending

title: Client overlay FPS and Mbps use incompatible cumulative counters and clock windows
description: Source-verified during L7 live streaming at d9fbdfe: src/client/main.c render_client_overlay computes FPS from lifetime frames_decoded divided by now-last_stats_ms, but last_stats_ms resets every 5 s in the CLI stats loop. FPS therefore spikes after each report rather than using a matching frame window. bitrate_mbps is total stream bytes_recv*8/1e6 with no elapsed-time divisor, so it is megabits transferred, not Mbps. Native counter/timestamp deltas are used in the matrix instead of trusting these displayed values. Reconnect also needs an explicit matching counter/clock baseline.
acceptance_criteria: Use a consistent monotonic interval and matching frame/byte deltas or per-connection totals/baseline. Cover reporting boundaries, zero elapsed and reconnect counter resets with pure arithmetic tests; verify displayed rates against observer counters.
notes: L13: implemented in local commit 868aa8c on md/l13-small-fixes (base 1d7daad). Separate src/client/rates.{c,h} computes FPS and Mbps from matching monotonic timestamp/frame/byte samples in a trailing 5-second window, sampling at most every 100ms. Disconnect explicitly clears state, and counter regressions establish new matching baselines. main.c only wires helper/removes obsolete reporting-clock argument; render.c untouched. Pure arithmetic tests compare rates with synthetic cumulative observer counters across 5s/10s report boundaries and duplicate renders; also cover changing rates, zero elapsed, idle gaps, reconnect/counter resets, clock wrap, large totals. Full macOS configure/build/test exit 0: 44/44 OK, no skips, client and all signer options enabled against dedicated nostrc cfcb86296. No new live display/stream observation performed. title: Encrypt direct-IP streams with keys bound to the Nostr-negotiated session
description: md-p4tl made direct-IP sessions authenticated: identity-pinned Nostr negotiation, then an expiring one-use session token proven on the TCP stream. Plain TCP still exposes the token and media to an on-path attacker (token theft/MITM, eavesdropping). Add transport encryption for direct TCP keyed from the negotiated session (e.g. a Noise/TLS handshake bound to the host and client Nostr keys or an exchanged ephemeral key in the NIP-44 session DM), so direct IP is as safe as the FIPS path.

title: host answers one session negotiation per process; a client that lost its stream cannot rebind without a host restart
description: Found by md-ah9.6. host/main.c latches ctx->session_requested on the first accepted request, and the stream token is one-use, so after a client's TCP stream drops (any transport blip) the client's reconnect loop (client/main.c, backoff to 30 s) sends fresh session requests that the still-running host never answers ('ERROR: timed out waiting for session accept' forever). Only a host process restart (restart policy / podman restart) recovers; the reference qualifies that path (client renegotiates with the restarted host over the mesh). A host that keeps listening for authorized session requests while idle, and re-arms binding after a disconnect, would make transport recovery automatic. Relates to md-trex (session list/kick) and md-3nv (multi-client streaming).
acceptance_criteria: After the stream of an accepted client drops, the same host process answers that client's next live session request and streams again; history/stale requests stay ignored (md-6ns).
close_reason: Merged md/l11-host-session (cbc24d3, bcd3f92): admission requires a usable frame/worker and refusals reach the client; host rearms after abandoned/refused sessions with replay fences and fresh tokens; macOS 45/45, ASan/TSan 6/6, Linux 4/4

comments.text:

Remaining gaps were abandoned/expired bind reservations leaving admission latched, expired/current-policy-refused renegotiations exiting the host, and a replay fence that remembered only the immediately previous request (A could reappear after B). Startup listening also had a one-shot 60-second window.

Fix: keep the same long-lived NIP-17 subscription; wait for live requests on its channel; rearm on binding reservation expiry and on stream EOF. host_next_session rechecks request freshness/current grants and --no-input, refuses just that negotiation and continues, recreates the correct tree-format agent before publishing a fresh UUID/one-use token. Keep every admitted ID through its entire freshness window in a bounded fail-closed cache; never evict an unexpired fence. Expected-client and account-owner checks, history refusal and token consumption remain intact. Capture snapshot/keyframe handoff also lets a recovered session receive its first frame on a static desktop. Atomic worker teardown prevents backend/negotiation errors from hanging the host join.

title: client --npub: dials once after link-level FIPS readiness; transient route loss fails the session
description: Found by md-ah9.6 (mesh-video-validation.md). md_fips_control_wait_peer_ready treats a show_peers entry with connectivity connected/active/stale plus link_id as READY, but after any fipsd (re)start the link flaps: crossing dials at startup (one link closed 'Other, close=5' and redialled ~0.3-0.6 s later) and a 'Restart, close=0' reconcile 3-11 s after a peer daemon restarts. The npub route on fips0 exists only while a link is up, so connects in those windows fail with ENETUNREACH or a lost SYN. The client then makes exactly one md_stream_connect_fips attempt; on the first connection it exits ('ERROR: FIPS connect failed'), and after a lost stream it renegotiates a NEW session, which a running host never answers (single negotiation per process). The reference works around it with a harness gate (raw TCP over fips0 until it succeeds; 11-30 s after a daemon restart). Second gap: with the peer daemon stopped, once the local daemon has timed out its link (~30 s), readiness still passes through the show_sessions fallback ('state=established'), so the client sends a session request instead of refusing (it still fails closed at the accept timeout). Fix direction: within the accepted session's bind window, retry the connect on ENETUNREACH/EHOSTUNREACH/timeout with backoff; require a usable route (link present, or established session plus route) for readiness.
acceptance_criteria: Client connect succeeds across a link flap in the bind window without renegotiating; readiness refuses when the peer's link is gone even if a stale session is listed; md-ah9.6 runs without its mesh-path gate.
notes: W6 commits 610f860 and 44b5b3e: fresh control snapshots plus cancellable exponential backoff (100..2000 ms), bounded dial attempts within accepted-token window, no renegotiation on transient dial failure. Stale established session without usable peer link no longer passes readiness. Inspected FIPS control API is one-shot, no readiness/route event subscription; retries use select-based backoff, not blind sleeps. Fake Unix control ready/link-gone/ready plus client dial seam verifies two dials and one accepted session; expiry/backoff clipping tested. ASan+UBSan 5/5, TSan 5/5; macOS 45 pass/1 live skip and nip5f 49 pass/1 live skip; Linux -j2 44/44. Conservative validity anchor request-publish-start +30 seconds because accept has no expiry: later accepts fail closed even if host issued token later. Inspected show_routing has no usable per-destination route proof; session-only/multihop readiness without peer link remains fail-closed. Live md-ah9.6 flap run without harness gate NOT performed; keep open for acceptance. No src/core/stream.c edits; no closure/push/merge.
close_reason: Merged md/w6-client: signal-driven session-wait shutdown (<5 s); overlay phases/grants/Disconnect/Quit (visually checked); cancellable exponential FIPS dial backoff with stale-session denial; macOS 49+1 skip, ASan/TSan 5/5, Linux 44/44. Live FIPS-flap acceptance not run.

title: uinput: first key can be lost after udev settle, before desktop consumer final open
description: Discovered by md-e3b disposable-VM acceptance run (L6, 2026-11-21). Ubuntu24.04.5 arm64 kernel6.8.0-147, libudev255, Xorg/libinput/Openbox on real virtio-GPU seat. udev settle itself works (matching keyboard/mouse eventN add in8–20ms; no timeout warning), but an X11 client injecting KEY_A press/release immediately after md_input_create loses both events on cycle14 after14 successes. Diagnostic with Xorg ptrace reproduces cycle0 with focus intact: md_input_create returns at monotonic549064.514ms, firstwrite549064.534ms; Xorg final /dev/input/event4 open about549065.129ms (0.595ms later). Xorg temporarily opens/closes during PreInit, then reopens, so a first IN_OPEN would not be a valid readiness ack. Need a designed desktop-consumer readiness contract (or honest capability/ready semantics) and an end-to-end regression, not sleeps, polling /proc, extended settle timeout, weakened tests, or declaring udev add sufficient. Current test_input live cells and ASan/UBSan each pass388checks because they do not assert first-key delivery. Full details retained in md-e3b notes. No source fix attempted outside the udevwait scope.

title: nostr.c allowlist: nostrc >= 5d1283a7c nip51 parse_list keeps metadesk-caps tags, so grants are duplicated and denied
description: Why: against nostrc master (5b3c987c8; behaviour from 5d1283a7c 'lossless social-list codecs') three tests fail once metadesk links (md-r4ia): capability grants private relay, access_cli private relay, mcp-proxy NIP-98 e2e private relay. nostr_nip51_parse_list used to keep only p/e/t/word/a/r tags; it now keeps every non-metadata tag as an entry, and returns NULL (ENOTSUP) for any tag with more than 3 fields. src/core/nostr.c (allowlist EVENT handler, ~line 864) assumes 'NIP-51's generic parser ignores application tags' and appends each metadesk-caps tag again, so entry_grant() sees grants == 2 and returns 0 (deny). Evidence (md-r4ia, macOS, private nostrc 5b3c987c8 build): a throwaway copy that skips the manual append when parse_list already yielded metadesk-caps entries passes 42/42 all-signers (unmodified: 39/42). What: make the allowlist load independent of whether parse_list keeps application tags (e.g. strip parser-provided metadesk-caps entries and keep metadesk's own arity-checked copies, or read grants only from raw tags); decide behaviour for >3-field tags (whole-list ENOTSUP vs today's per-tag invalid grant) and keep the 'trailing payload' case at 0. Must pass against both the shared (da2e4d62b / 120ca9672) and master trees.
notes: Fixed in 92d5c18 (branch fix/md-jqnz-nip51-grant-parse). Allowlist decoded from raw tags (allowlist_from_event), no nostr_nip51_parse_list; first d = address; p any arity; metadesk-caps arity!=3 retained invalid (deny that pk); other tags ignored and not republished. list_append_copy no longer calls nostr_nip51_list_add_entry (version-dependent failure contract). Gates all green: macOS shared 120ca9672 37/37 + 42/42, private master 5b3c987c8 37/37 + 42/42; VM shared da2e4d62b 36/36 + 41/41, private master 5b3c987c8 36/36 + 41/41, each parallel and serial. Follow-up: md-gex4.
close_reason: Allowlist decoded from raw tags independent of nostrc nip51 tag policy; gates green on shared and master trees (macOS + VM)

title: macOS: libnsync's clock_gettime shadows libSystem, so CLOCK_MONOTONIC reads wall time project-wide
description: Why: Homebrew libnsync 1.30 exports _clock_gettime, and on macOS it ignores the clock id and returns gettimeofday wall time. ld binds each undefined symbol to the first dylib in link order that exports it, and nsync (dep_nsync, meson.build:183) comes before libSystem. So libmetadesk and every tool or test linking it resolve clock_gettime to libnsync. Check with: nm -m build/libmetadesk.0.dylib | grep clock_gettime, which shows '(from libnsync)'. Found during md-6c4f: tools/capture_frame's CLOCK_MONOTONIC read returned 1.795e18 ns (epoch). Impact: every clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) on macOS is wall time, so NTP slews and steps and manual clock changes move deadlines and timeouts. Affected: io_util.h, stream.c (2 sites), fips_control.c (2), host/main.c (3), client/main.c, mcp_resources.c, the tests test_mcp/test_host_binding/test_atspi/mcp_proxy_host_fixture, and tools atspi_dump/encode_roundtrip. Linux is unaffected: Linux libnsync only imports clock_gettime@GLIBC. What: either (a) give one shared md_monotonic_ns() (io_util.h) that uses clock_gettime_nsec_np(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) on __APPLE__ and route every site through it (md_capture_clock_ns in capture.c already does this for frame timestamps), or (b) fix link resolution on darwin so libSystem wins, e.g. link -lSystem ahead of nsync, then verify with nm -m. Add a regression check that the monotonic clock is not wall time (test_capture's test_frame_clock has the pattern).
close_reason: Fixed in d730d08 on fix/md-5aua-monotonic-clock (unmerged). (a) md_time.{h,c}: md_monotonic_ns()/md_now_ms()/md_cond_*. Every caller converted; md_capture_clock_ns aliases it. (b) darwin links -lSystem before libnsync, and nm -m shows from libSystem. tests/test_time.c plus the darwin nm test fail when either fix is reverted. macOS 36/36, Linux 36/36 parallel and serial. Follow-up: md-l4f4 (nostr.c wait_history).

title: SendInput targets the primary monitor only; wrong with --capture-output on a non-primary output
description: Why: md-346 added MdCaptureConfig.output / --capture-output so DXGI can capture any attached output, but input_sendinput.cpp maps client coordinates with MOUSEEVENTF_ABSOLUTE normalised to screen_w/h and no MOUSEEVENTF_VIRTUALDESK, which addresses the primary monitor. Capturing a non-primary output therefore sends clicks to the wrong place. What: expose the captured output's virtual-desktop rect from the capture HAL (e.g. an origin in MdCaptureCtx or a getter; DxgiState.output_desc.DesktopCoordinates has it), pass it into MdInputConfig, and normalise against the virtual desktop (SM_X/Y/CX/CYVIRTUALSCREEN) with MOUSEEVENTF_VIRTUALDESK. Test with the SendInput recorder (never inject real input).
close_reason: Committed on feat/windows-w65-dbg-246: DXGI publishes the physical output rect via md-xat's md_capture_get_output_rect; SendInput maps with md_input_map_to_output and normalises across the physical virtual desktop with MOUSEEVENTF_VIRTUALDESK (pixel-centre, exact round-trip). Recorder + synthetic GetSystemMetrics tests; clang/MSVC/session 0/console/macOS green apart from pre-existing flake md-4dsa.

comments.author: Biz
comments.text: Coordination from md-xat (branch feat/md-xat-sck-output, macOS). It adds HAL plumbing that DXGI can reuse instead of inventing parallel names. (1) capture.h: typedef MdCaptureRect {int32_t x,y; uint32_t width,height}, MdCaptureCtx.output_rect (backend sets it in start), and md_capture_get_output_rect(ctx,&rect). DXGI can fill it from output_desc.DesktopCoordinates. (2) input.h: MdInputConfig gains int32_t output_x, output_y and uint32_t output_width, output_height, plus a pure md_input_map_to_output(cfg,x,y,&gx,&gy) (clamp + offset/scale into global desktop space). (3) host/main.c: copies the rect into input_cfg next to screen_width/height. (4) input.c: md_input_execute_action now treats click coordinates as GLOBAL (accessibility) coordinates. With output bounds set, it inverse-maps them to frame space and refuses points off the captured output, because the stream-mode agent shares the host MdInput. SendInput can map gx/gy to VIRTUALDESK normalised coordinates. Expect overlap in capture.h, input.h/input.c and that host/main.c hunk.

title: Client accepts a stale session_accept replayed from relay history
description: Found by md-ah9.11. The client's gift-wrap subscription uses since=now-2d (NIP-59 window) and takes the first session_accept DM from the host; it does not correlate the accept with its current request. Against a relay that retains history, a second negotiation for the same host/client pair (new host process) replays the previous session's accept: client logged 'session accepted (id=0929f5ec...)' while the live host had reserved 6531447f...; client sent the stale proof, host 'rejected unproven client #1', client 'ERROR: failed to send session info'. Fails closed (no auth bypass), but repeat sessions within two days fail on retaining relays. Related deferred P3.8 request-ID/correlation work (docs/stream-binding.md); no bead tracked it. md-ah9.11 used a fresh private relay per cell to avoid it.
acceptance_criteria: Client only accepts a session_accept bound to its own current request (request id/nonce or rumor freshness); a test replays an old accept over a retaining relay and the next negotiation still succeeds
close_reason: Fixed on fix/md-6ns-stale-accept (1706481, rebased on master c6d6ba1): request_id/issued_at/expires_at correlation (v1, session-v2 field shapes); client accepts only its current request's answer; host answers only live (post-EOSE) fresh requests without latching on history; dedup live-upgrade for history-first copies. Retaining-relay + two-relay tests and second real host/client e2e on same relay pass on macOS/Linux/ASan. Follow-ups: md-cdz (container same-relay cell), md-tiy (fips_addr UBSan).

title: NIP-5F signer cannot decrypt NIP-17 session requests: nostrc client returns JSON-escaped strings
description: Found by md-ah9.11. nostrc nips/nip5f/src/core/sock_client.c nostr_nip5f_client_nip44_decrypt (and nip44_encrypt) strip the surrounding quotes of the JSON string result but never unescape it. Any plaintext containing a double quote comes back as {\"... so a NIP-5F-backed host rejects every NIP-17 gift wrap: '[json] event parse failed: compact: expected , or closing delimiter (offset 2)' then 'nostr: DM rejected: invalid-seal'. A server cannot avoid this (JSON strings must escape quotes). Same code at the VM nostrc build da2e4d62 and local nostrc 120ca9672. docs/accounts.md lists nip5f as a host/client backend, so NIP-5F hosts/clients cannot negotiate sessions; access CLI signing works (no decrypt). The md-pss access_cli private relay test never decrypts, so it does not catch this.
acceptance_criteria: nostrc NIP-5F client JSON-unescapes string results (or parses result with a JSON parser); a metadesk test negotiates a host session through a NIP-5F signer whose decrypted seal contains quotes
notes: nostrc side merged in nostrc master f2753a2ec (nip5f client parses results with the JSON parser). Remaining: metadesk NIP-5F host-session test after shared nostrc builds are rebuilt.
close_reason: Completed upstream by f2753a2ec and metadesk regression 8cbb8dd: NIP-5F host session quoted seal uses private Unix signer/relay, real NIP-17 host admission and correlated acceptance/token. Observer proves decrypted kind13 seal and kind14 rumor contain quoted JSON. Passes macOS/VM and ASan/TSan; selected build-tree adapter now overrides stale ABI-compatible installed adapter.

title: MCP: gate action tools on the principal's input grant (per-request caps)
description: md-ah9.3 admits NIP-98 MCP principals whose host-allowlist grant includes agent, but MCP has no per-principal tool gating: an admitted principal gets the whole tool surface (actions unless --no-input/no input backend). For video sessions, agent without input hides actions (docs/access.md). The MCP HTTP authorizer should return the principal's capability mask (static/bearer = host policy), and tools/call of non-read tools (mcp_tools.c read_kind==0) must require MD_CAP_INPUT, with tools/list filtered per principal. Needs a caller-context variant of md_mcp_server_handle_message_with_sink. See docs/mcp-auth.md 'Scope note'.
acceptance_criteria: agent-only principal: tools/list has no action tools and tools/call of an action returns is_error naming input; agent,input principal unchanged; bearer/static unchanged; tests in test_mcp_http.c + e2e
close_reason: Done in 4b7de85 (feat/md-5km-mcp-input-grant, not pushed/merged). Rules: live host-allowlist NIP-98 principals get their current v1 grant, read afresh on every request; admission needs agent; read tools/resources need agent; the 9 action tools need agent+input. Static npub/file, bearer, credential-less loopback and stdio get all caps, still subject to --no-input/input readiness (operator credentials with no grant vocabulary; keeps existing deployments). Agent-only: tools/list omits actions; tools/call returns isError 'requires the 'input' grant' with no handler run. Grant changes apply to the next request; SSE recheck needs agent; session-info is caller-narrowed. Gates: macOS meson test 35/35 (all signer backends); Linux VM 36 OK + 1 opt-in skip (access session e2e), parallel (-j2/2 procs) and serial; ASan+UBSan (LSan on Linux) MCP tests 5/5 on both. nostr-protocol-smells diff review: clean. Follow-up: md-ht7 (tools/list_changed).

title: Upstream report: libatspi 2.52 get_application pending call is not released by atspi_exit
description: Follow-up to md-x16: report to GNOME at-spi2-core upstream. AT_SPI2_CORE_2_52_0 atspi/atspi-misc.c get_application (427/434) calls dbus_connection_send_with_reply(GetApplicationBusAddress), retains the caller-owned DBusPendingCall reference and installs handle_get_bus_address with no destroy notifier. Only that callback unrefs it. handle_get_bus_address likewise creates GetItems pending calls whose reference is only released by handle_get_items. Neither cleanup()/atspi_exit nor atspi_application_dispose tracks/cancels/unrefs these requests. If connection teardown prevents callback dispatch, the retained pending call keeps its connection/error reply/timeout allocations alive. Ubuntu 24.04 aarch64 libatspi build-id d0fdcf72be49abfb6f06898b37e3708b3eb00df3 debug info maps offsets 0x17258/0x1727c to get_application (not GetItems); caller _atspi_ref_accessible at 0x1bd10. Baseline 15/1000 mode2 failures, 871 bytes/6 indirect allocations, predates md-dzm. Source https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/at-spi2-core/-/blob/AT_SPI2_CORE_2_52_0/atspi/atspi-misc.c . Attach independent libatspi-only reproducer and diagnostic results from md-x16 before upstream submission. Public API provides no handle or pending-call drain/cancel operation; do not change metadesk dispatcher lifetime or add timer-based workaround. Verify upstream fix then remove private-test-only exact-frame LSan suppression.
close_reason: Invalid: not an upstream bug. The stranded get_application pending call is caused by metadesk calling libatspi off its dispatch thread (md-x16, fixed in b0f7f26 by walking on the default context). Single-threaded libatspi use cannot complete the call between send_with_reply and set_notify. No suppression or upstream report needed.

title: Linux VM MCP HTTP test has fragile port/deadline gates
description: Observed during md-pss qualification on 192.168.64.3 (Ubuntu arm64), all signer backends enabled. Default parallel full suite: MCP HTTP+SSE transport timed out at 15.15s (34 other tests passed). Serial full suite: test_mcp_http.c:1178 http != NULL failed, then auth_status/connect/read-budget assertions at 1182-1197 (15/625 failed); 34 other tests passed. Untouched 5966e40 baseline built separately under ~/wt-pss/baseline passed the targeted test in 14.57s, close to its existing 15s Meson timeout. No MCP or AT-SPI source/test edits in md-pss. Investigate fixed/dynamic port reservation and test timing; do not simply relax production authorization deadlines. Gate logs /tmp/md-pss-linux-tests.log, /tmp/md-pss-linux-serial.log, /tmp/md-pss-baseline-test.log on VM.
close_reason: Fixed in 18fe3af. Root cause: (1) slowness ~14 s vs a 15 s timeout: each case's shutdown waited out the accept loop's 1 s select poll (13 x ~1.0 s); (2) failures: the fixed port range 18710+ meant any foreign listener or concurrent checkout caused create to fail, and the NULL server then cascaded (15/631). Fix: test-only ephemeral_port plus md_mcp_http_port(), a wake connection on shutdown, and REQUIRE_HTTP. Production paths are unchanged (CLIENT_READ_TIMEOUT_SEC=2, shutdown semantics). Linux VM full suite --repeat 200: parallel (-j2) 6800 OK/0 fail/0 timeout, MCP HTTP min 3.28/med 3.30/max 3.41 s; serial 6800 OK/0 fail/0 timeout, MCP HTTP med 3.34/max 3.41 s (the 200 skips are the access session e2e test). Netns collision proof with ::1:18712 held: baseline 3e5c926 rc=1, 15/631 fail from :1178, then blocked 310 s; fixed 649/649 in 3.33 s. macOS meson test 29/29, targeted repeat 30/30. Follow-up md-wl5 (test_stream/test_agent fixed ports). Evidence: /tmp/md-e65-evidence on the Mac.

title: AT-SPI host bus-loss cleanup intermittently leaks libatspi pending calls under LSan
description: Found while qualifying md-dzm on Linux VM (atspi 2.52.0 / GLib 2.80). Unsuppressed ASan/LSan occasionally aborts host mode2 after its otherwise-correct accessibility bus-loss shutdown: LeakSanitizer871 bytes in6 indirect allocations, pending call from _atspi_ref_accessible / GetItems, plus libdbus message buffers. Confirmed independent of md-dzm lifecycle fix: host-only diagnostic using original5966e40 backend shared library (copied before changes) and ASan-instrumented fixture/host reproduces the identical871-byte leak; logs /tmp/dzm-baseline-host-lsan-1000.log (will preserve local before VM cleanup). Original backend reproduces, and no suppression or leak-check disabling is committed. Investigate upstream pending-call cancellation/ref ownership on disconnect/atspi_exit; do not confuse this with md-dzm stale-source dispatch crash/hang. Live GNOME bus untouched and calculator verified after batches.
close_reason: Fixed in b0f7f26 (branch fix/md-x16-atspi-pending-leak, awaiting review/merge): tree walk serialized on the default GLib context; metadesk-owned race, no suppression.

comments.author: Biz
comments.text: Baseline confirmation complete: original5966e40 backend shared library + ASan fixture/host, host mode2 only, 2-way concurrency:15/1000 runs fail with the same871-byte/6-allocation libatspi/libdbus LSan pending-call leak (preceding100-run batch0/100). No backend source fix loaded in those hosts: LD_LIBRARY_PATH=~/wt-dzm/before-lib contains a copied pre-change libmetadesk.so.0. Artifact preserved locally at /tmp/md-dzm-evidence/dzm-baseline-host-lsan-1000.log after cleanup. AddressSanitizer access-safety gate is run separately with detect_leaks=0; no suppression committed.

comments.author: Biz
comments.text: Final baseline proof:15/1000 host-only LSan failures using untouched5966e40 backend shared library with ASan-instrumented fixture/host (initial100/100 clean demonstrates intermittency). Identical871 bytes/6 allocations. Evidence preserved on macOS under /tmp/md-dzm-evidence/dzm-baseline-host-lsan-1000.log plus unsuppressed final report dzm-final-asan.log. VM ~/wt-dzm and task temp files removed. md-dzm fix cfa4ac2 passes200/200 ASan address tests only with detect_leaks=0; no suppression/LSan disabling committed.

comments.author: Biz
comments.text: Root cause (metadesk-owned, not libatspi): atspi_get_tree ran libatspi on the MCP thread while md-atspi-events dispatched libatspi's connection on the default context. atspi_get_desktop -> _atspi_ref_accessible -> get_application (at-spi2-core 2.52 atspi-misc.c:402-436) send_with_reply(GetApplicationBusAddress) then set_notify(handle_get_bus_address); libdbus completes only in dispatch and set_notify on a completed call never runs it (dbus 1.14.10 dbus-pending-call.c:649), so a dispatch in that window leaks the pending call + reply (6 allocs at _atspi_ref_accessible+0x1bd10; 871 B with cached disconnect error, 727 B with real reply). dbind also dispatches from the calling thread when g_main_depth()==0. Fix b0f7f26: walk via atspi_invoke_sync on the context. Deterministic regression: in-test set_notify interposer, master fails fixture mode 0 (1 of 2 off-context), fixed passes. Unsuppressed LSan host mode 2: fixed 0/1000; fixed + 2ms pre-set_notify delay shim 0/1000; master + shim 199/200 (all late-notify). Linux full suite 30/30 parallel(2)+serial; ASan a11y x50 100/100 0 LSan; macOS 28/29 (only md-e65 HTTP flake). Previous attempt's LSan suppression discarded (its own master baseline was 0/1000; ownership claim wrong). Evidence /tmp/md-x16-evidence/README.txt on macOS. Live bus inode 5037 / calculator 743316 unchanged; VM ~/wt-x16 removed.

title: Investigate parsed relay EVENT leak during role-bridge teardown
description: Supplemental Linux ASan/LSan runtime finding in private md-70v.3 fixture: after publishing/receiving a kind-30000 allowlist and immediately switching/destroying role bridges, LSan reported 586 bytes in 16 allocations, direct 64-byte nostr_event_new allocated by nostr_envelope_deserialize_compact -> nostr_envelope_parse -> relay message_loop; all stacks in linked nostrc code. Exact ownership/root cause not yet proven. Core accounts and queued-role-cancellation ASan cases passed. macOS ASan passed (LSan unavailable there). No leak suppressions applied. Fixture is being synchronized on verified echo consumption before controlled teardown; investigate transport/subscription shutdown with queued EVENTs independently, rather than assuming one green sanitizer run disproves the observation. Reproduce using all signer backends on Linux VM ~/wt-70v-3 build-asan, tests account startup roles + private relay restore; full trace recorded in run handoff. No nostrc/sibling checkout edits authorized in md-70v.3.
notes: Root cause now source-verified: nostr-simple-pool.h documents that middleware owns incoming->event; simplepool.c only frees events when no middleware exists. Metadesk md_nostr_event_handler never freed the transferred event on success/rejection/stop. Fixed in this worktree using a single owning callback shim around borrowed event routing; no nostrc changes or suppressions. Private fixture now explicitly awaits verified allowlist echo consumption before testing stale-cache revocation. Pending repeated Linux ASan/LSan verification before closure.
close_reason: Fixed bridge middleware event ownership (pool transfers incoming->event; now freed on every routing/rejection/stop path). Verified final macOS ASan 3/3 and Linux ASan/LSan 9/9 across three repetitions, no suppressions; full suites macOS 29/29 all-backends and Linux 30/30. No nostrc checkout changes.

title: fipsd packaged peer example uses a schema rejected by the daemon
description: Found during md-ah9.5 against nostrc 5d09cab9183a09a0b0b88d89c20495b55beb2a50. fipsd/packaging/common/fips.yaml suggests peers entries with address and transport at peer level. src/config/peer.c instead requires addresses: [{transport: udp, addr: HOST:PORT}]. Enabling the shipped example produces unknown configuration key peers[0].address / peers[0].transport, followed by fatal must specify at least one address. Reproduced with built fipsd 0.1.0 in rootless Podman 4.9.3 on Ubuntu 24.04 aarch64. Correcting only the adapter YAML to the actual schema starts TUN and establishes the link. Follow up in nostrc; no external source changes made in this task.
notes: nostrc fix committed (not merged): 36cf3aa99 on land/md-ebm-uzf (nostrc-vxvqx). Both shipped fips.yaml examples (common, windows) use addresses: [{transport, addr}]; FipsdConfigExample_{common,windows} load each through fipsd_config_load as shipped and with all commented settings enabled. fipsd -> 0.1.1 (PATCH after fipsd-v0.1.0).
close_reason: Fixed in nostrc master f2753a2ec: fipsd shipped examples use addresses:[{transport,addr}], loader tests added; fipsd 0.1.1

title: Windows UIA: qualify actual OS lock/disconnect delivery at the console
description: Follow-up release qualification for md-yre. Real interactive desktop tree and subscribe/unsubscribe, session-0 rejection, synthetic WM_WTSSESSION_CHANGE through registered listener, injected root provider errors, late callback and concurrent teardown tests pass. Actual OS-generated lock/disconnect delivery has not been exercised because this locks/disconnects the active UTM console and needs coordinated user unlock. Steps: build with tools/win/build-uia-harness.sh; with user logged in at VM console and CLANGARM64 bin on PATH, launch build-win-uia/test_uia_liveness.exe --wait-for-loss in the console or an Interactive scheduled task; within 30 seconds use Win+L, capture ALL UIA LIVENESS TESTS PASSED and exit 0, unlock console; repeat separately with session disconnect if needed. Stop/unregister any scheduled task and remove temp scripts/output. Also check startup while locked returns disconnected. See tools/win/README.md. Full supervised MCP Windows product runtime remains unavailable until existing Windows product dependencies are resolved; harness proves backend lifetime, not a full host integration run.
acceptance_criteria: Record OS-generated lock/disconnect loss and locked-startup results, exact Windows version/session, cleanup and user-console restoration.
notes:
Design note (orchestrator, 2026-11-18): md-yre treats WTS_SESSION_LOCK as desktop loss, so an MCP-mode host exits on screen lock and its restart fails the startup check until unlock (consistent with md-ah9 Q4: exit on loss plus restart policy). If a host should survive a lock, model lock as temporarily unavailable rather than lost. Decide when qualifying real OS lock delivery here.

title: Windows UIA liveness reports allocation rather than desktop availability
description: Found while fixing md-ah9.15. src/core/a11y_uia.cpp:uia_is_connected returns st && st->automation != nullptr; it never observes UIA/desktop loss. A COM automation pointer surviving a desktop/session transition cannot establish current accessibility readiness. macOS checks AXIsProcessTrusted on each predicate call; AT-SPI now watches bus disconnect. A safe UIA event/failure-based transition needs Windows live tests and COM apartment/lifetime validation; deliberately not changed in this macOS/Linux task.
acceptance_criteria: Qualify desktop/session or UIA provider loss on Windows; reflect loss with a cheap thread-safe predicate and verify supervised MCP shutdown without freeing an in-flight COM call.
notes:
Implemented in local-only commit 21fbe051a8c0ef51fa2e47bf86fc5d41b4c21ad1 on fix/md-yre-uia-liveness; not pushed or merged. Independent init-to-destroy hidden-window WTS monitor latches lock/disconnect/logoff loss with Interlocked predicate; validates input desktop/session at startup (session 0 false). Root access observes RPC_E_DISCONNECTED/UIA_E_ELEMENTNOTAVAILABLE/CO_E_OBJNOTCONNECTED/RPC server unavailable; no child-provider failure treated globally. Root probing occurs on root access, not a polling timer; silent idle provider failure has no separate heartbeat. COM MTA enforced; worker tree calls join MTA. Destroy closes admission and drains active AND queued tree callers before freeing proxies/state; handler-owned detach lock protects late COM callbacks. title: Windows live UIA run: newline labels break compact format; UIA control-type gaps + Header→HEADING mis-map
description:
Why: the first interactive Windows desktop walk through metadesk (UTM Win11 ARM64, 250 nodes, atspi_dump --compact) surfaced: (1) labels containing CR/LF (taskbar Clock 'Clock 4:51 PM\n<LRM>11/16/2026', OneDrive and Network tray buttons; 3 labels) are emitted verbatim by compact_node(), so a single node spills across lines and the line-based compact format (spec §3.3.2) becomes ambiguous — platform-neutral, any backend can produce multi-line accessible names. (2) 5 nodes with role 'unknown': a11y_uia.cpp MD_UIA_ROLES lacks Thumb, Separator, TitleBar, HeaderItem, Calendar, Custom, AppBar, SemanticZoom. (3) UIA_HeaderControlTypeId is mapped to MD_A11Y_ROLE_HEADING, but UIA Header is the container of HeaderItems (column header row), not a heading — same class of bug as the AT-SPI 'header' alias fixed in md-eiy. Encoding was verified correct (UTF-8 C2 B0 / E2 80 8E bytes); the garbling seen was PowerShell 5.1 display only.

What: (a) compact serializer: replace control characters (< 0x20, incl. CR/LF/TAB) in labels with a single space; JSON unchanged (cJSON escapes). Unit test. (b) UIA: add the missing control types to MD_UIA_ROLES (Separator→SEPARATOR, TitleBar→LABEL to match the AT-SPI 'title bar' alias, HeaderItem→COLUMN_HEADER, Calendar→CALENDAR, AppBar→TOOL_BAR, SemanticZoom→LIST, Thumb/Custom→UNKNOWN explicitly), fix Header→PANEL, and log unmapped control types once per distinct id (mirror AXUI md-eiy). (c) Re-run the interactive Windows walk and the live suite: 0 multi-line compact nodes, unknown roles only for deliberate UNKNOWN mappings.
acceptance_criteria: Compact output never contains a newline inside a node line (unit test); Windows interactive dump shows no unmapped UIA control types except explicit UNKNOWN; Header no longer emits HDG; macOS + Linux + Windows suites pass.
close_reason: Merged to master. Compact labels sanitized (control chars -> single space, test added); UIA table: Separator/TitleBar/HeaderItem/Calendar/AppBar/SemanticZoom mapped, Thumb/Custom explicit UNKNOWN, Header->PANEL, once-per-type unmapped log. Verified live on Windows interactive session: 0 split lines (was 3), 2 unknown roles (was 5, both deliberate), 0 unmapped types logged; macOS 22/22, Linux 22/22 + live AT-SPI, Windows clang 0 diagnostics + MSVC /W4 clean.

title: AT-SPI backend leaves NULL holes in node->states for unmapped AtspiState values
description:
Why: src/core/a11y_atspi.c extract_states() sizes node->states to the full AtspiStateSet length (:75-76, calloc) but only strdup()s a name for the 17 AtspiState values in its switch (:87-109); every other state (ATSPI_STATE_HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, OPAQUE, MANAGES_DESCENDANTS, RESIZABLE, TRANSIENT, ...) leaves node->states[i] == NULL while state_count still counts it. Found on the Linux UTM VM (Ubuntu 24.04, GNOME 46) with MD_A11Y_LIVE_TESTS=1 ./build/test_atspi: 460 of 11776 checks fail at tests/test_atspi.c:372 (md_a11y_state_lookup(NULL) -> UNKNOWN) on a 15-node desktop; never reproducible on macOS. Consumers that iterate states[] without a NULL guard (any strcmp/cJSON_CreateString path) are at risk of a NULL deref; md_a11y_matches guards it, others need checking. Pre-existing — the pre-md-eiy code had the same 'if (name) states[i] = strdup(name)' pattern.

What: compact the array — append only mapped names and set state_count to the number appended (or realloc/shrink), never leave holes; optionally map a few more AT-SPI states that exist in a11y_vocab.h. Add a unit test with a fake state set containing unmapped values asserting no NULL entries and state_count == mapped count. Verify on the Linux VM: full suite + MD_A11Y_LIVE_TESTS=1 test_atspi must report 0 unknown states.
acceptance_criteria: Live AT-SPI test on the Linux VM reports 0 'unknown state' and PASSED; unit test covers unmapped states; no NULL entries possible in node->states from any backend.
close_reason: Merged to master as 623349a. extract_states compacts the array (no NULL holes); Linux-only seam md_atspi_extract_states + unit test with synthetic AtspiStateSet. Verified on the Linux UTM VM: 22/22, live AT-SPI PASSED 11326 checks / 0 unknown states (was 460 failures). macOS 22/22.

title: MCP bridge destroy does not unsubscribe a11y change callback (use-after-free on teardown)
description:
Why: md_mcp_bridge_create() registers md_mcp_a11y_change_cb with the bridge (or its resource ctx) as userdata via md_a11y_subscribe_changes(config->a11y, ...) (src/core/mcp_bridge.c:98). md_mcp_bridge_destroy() (mcp_bridge.c:173-) tears down transports, tool contexts, server, and agent but never detaches that subscription, and src/core/a11y.h exposes no unsubscribe API at all (only int (*subscribe_changes) in the vtable and md_a11y_subscribe_changes). Because the host keeps the MdA11yCtx alive and destroys it only after the bridge (src/host/main.c ~:790), any backend change event delivered in that window — AT-SPI event, AXObserver notification, UIA COM event — invokes the callback with a freed bridge/resource pointer. Surfaced by the md-52m engineer while adding snapshot invalidation to the callback (which widens the window since the callback now touches the snapshot too).

What: (1) add md_a11y_unsubscribe_changes(MdA11yCtx*, MdA11yChangeCb, void*) (or make subscribe return a handle) to a11y.h and implement it in all three backends — a11y_atspi.c (atspi_event_listener_deregister), a11y_axui.m (AXObserverRemoveNotification / CFRunLoopRemoveSource), a11y_uia.cpp (RemoveAutomationEventHandler / RemoveFocusChangedEventHandler); the backends must guarantee no callback runs after unsubscribe returns (join or synchronize with the dispatch thread). (2) Call it first thing in md_mcp_bridge_destroy(), before freeing anything the callback can touch. (3) Test in tests/test_mcp.c with the fake backend: after bridge destroy, firing a fake change event must not invoke the callback (use a counting hook).
acceptance_criteria: a11y.h has an unsubscribe API implemented by all three backends; md_mcp_bridge_destroy unsubscribes before teardown; test asserts no callback after destroy; all tests pass.
close_reason: Merged to master as 39f2458 (93d07b9, 05b5c0d, 9a0240e). md_a11y_unsubscribe_changes with in-flight drain; bridge detaches first. UIA backend change uncompiled on macOS — verify on a Windows build. 22/22 unit + live AX test pass

title: Spike: run metadesk host/client inside containers (headless capture, input, FIPS, OCI runtime)
description:
Why: metadesk should run inside containers — both a containerized HOST (expose a container's desktop/app to agents + humans) and a containerized CLIENT (esp. agent/MCP). This is a runtime/architecture problem distinct from the packaging-format spike (md-kb7); md-kb7 only owns 'publish OCI images' as a distribution channel, this spike owns 'make it actually work headless in a container'. Strongly aligned with the AI-agent use case: a sandboxed container workload an agent drives headlessly via MCP + a11y.

What (spike — prototype + recommend):
- HOST in container:
  - Capture without a physical display: headless Wayland compositor (wlroots/cage/gnome headless), Xvfb+X11 capture, or a nested compositor; vs host-socket passthrough.
  - PipeWire + xdg-desktop-portal inside the container (own instance vs bind-mounting host sockets), ScreenCast consent in a non-interactive/headless context (restore_token, or portal backend that auto-grants).
  - Input injection without bare-metal /dev/uinput + CAP: wlroots virtual-pointer/virtual-keyboard protocols, ydotool, or inject into the nested compositor; device passthrough tradeoffs.
  - AT-SPI accessibility bus inside the container.
  - FIPS: TUN in the container netns (CAP_NET_ADMIN, /dev/net/tun) vs a FIPS sidecar sharing the network namespace; or direct IP only.
- CLIENT in container:
  - Agent/MCP client (no display) — primary, mostly networking.
  - Human client with display — GPU/display passthrough (DRI, Wayland/X socket) or stream-to-browser; likely out of initial scope.
- Runtime targets: Docker, Podman (incl. rootless), Kubernetes (Pod spec, securityContext, device plugins, service exposure), systemd-nspawn.
- Security: minimize capabilities, rootless where possible, document the privilege each feature requires.
- Reference deployments: Dockerfile(s)/compose + a k8s manifest for the headless-agent host scenario.

Deliverable: a design doc (docs/designs/) with a recommended headless-capture + input + FIPS architecture per runtime, a capability/privilege matrix, the consent/permission story for non-interactive hosts, example Dockerfile/compose/k8s manifests, and a phased plan with spin-off issues. Coordinate with md-kb7 (OCI images as a channel) and md-5zi (add container cells to the E2E matrix).

2026-11-16: all §7.4 decisions made — Q1 throwaway bundle; Q2 Host/Origin + bearer + NIP-98 (§7.7); Q3 explicit 127.0.0.1; Q4 exit on a11y loss + restart policy; Q5 unregister tools + is_error backstop; Q6 Tier A + proxy (W3) then binary-session (W3v); Q7 K8s deferred to Tier B. Work items filed as md-ah9.1–.14 (index in plan §1.1). md-ah9 itself = P0 (deploy/containers drafts still to do).

title: Spike: cross-platform distribution packaging — no-build-from-source install on all major platforms (incl. Omarchy)
description:
Why: today metadesk is source-only (meson + ninja, with a hand-built nostrc tree and system FFmpeg/SDL2/libyuv/etc.). Adoption requires simple, no-compile installs — users should get a signed, pre-built package per platform, not a build environment. ('non-FYC' = not 'fetch-your-compiler'/from-source.)

What (spike — survey, prototype, and recommend; not full build-out):
- Define per-platform packaging + delivery channels:
  - macOS: signed + notarized .app in a .dmg; Homebrew cask. (metadesk-host + metadesk-client.)
  - Windows: signed installer (MSI/EXE or MSIX) + winget manifest.
  - Linux (distro-agnostic): Flatpak on Flathub (portal/PipeWire/ScreenCast fit GNOME well) and/or AppImage for portable use.
  - Debian/Ubuntu: .deb + apt repo/PPA.
  - Fedora/RHEL: .rpm + Copr/dnf repo.
  - Arch + Omarchy: AUR package (pacman); validate on Omarchy's Hyprland/Wayland stack (xdg-desktop-portal-hyprland for ScreenCast, wlroots input).
- Dependency strategy: bundle vs system for FFmpeg, SDL2, libyuv, secp256k1, libwebsockets, cJSON, libb2, nostrc (currently an uninstalled build-tree dep — needs a proper installable/vendored story), and the GUI toolkit if the UX spike (md-70v) adds one.
- External runtime deps that are NOT bundled: the FIPS daemon (document how users get it per platform) and screen-capture permissions/portals per OS.
- Code signing / notarization / reproducibility; versioning; auto-update strategy (Sparkle/winget/Flatpak/repo updates).
- CI/CD: a release pipeline that builds + signs + publishes artifacts for every target from tags.

Deliverable: a design doc (docs/designs/) with a recommended channel per platform, the dependency-bundling decision matrix, signing/notarization plan, auto-update approach, a CI release-pipeline sketch, and a phased rollout with spin-off issues. Include an explicit Omarchy/Hyprland validation checklist. Coordinate with md-70v (UX/toolkit choice affects packaging) and md-5zi (per-platform E2E).

title: Spike: host/client management UX — identity/keys, connecting to hosts, address book, parity with remote-desktop tools
description:
Why: the current client/host are CLI-only (npub/IP args, op:// secrets, manual signer flags). To be usable like mainstream remote-desktop packages (RustDesk, Parsec, AnyDesk, RealVNC, Moonlight), metadesk needs real management UX for identity and connections on BOTH ends.

What (spike — explore + propose, not full build):
- Identity & key handling: generate/import/rotate Nostr keypairs (nsec/npub), secure at-rest storage (keychain/1Password/secret-service), unlock flow, display npub/fingerprint, signer selection (NIP-46 bunker, NIP-55L, NIP-5F, local).
- Connect-to-host flow: enter/scan an npub or IP, trust-on-first-use prompt, saved credentials, connection status/errors surfaced clearly (FIPS readiness, auth, route).
- Host address book: named saved hosts (npub/IP, last-connected, tags, per-host capabilities/notes), favorites, quick-connect, import/export.
- Host side: approve/deny incoming clients, NIP-51 allowlist management UI, session list/kick, per-client granted capabilities.
- General parity: settings (resolution/bitrate/fps), reconnect UX, clipboard, multi-monitor selection, in-overlay connection manager.

Deliverable: a design doc (docs/designs/) covering IA, flows, where it lives (ImGui overlay vs separate GTK/native app vs both), data model for the address book, security model for key storage, and a phased implementation plan with issues to spin off. Survey 2-3 comparable tools for UX patterns.
design:
Nostr-native constraint: prefer Nostr protocol primitives over bespoke mechanisms wherever practical.

- NIP-05: human-readable host identifiers (user@domain) that resolve to the host npub, so users connect to 'host@example.com' instead of a raw npub. Support NIP-05 verification/display in the connect flow and address book.
- NIP-51 (lists): use standard list events for the host allowlist/approved clients and for the client-side host address book / favorites / tags (e.g. categorized people/relay/app-specific sets) rather than a local-only format. Lists sync across a user's devices via relays.
- NIP-78 (application-specific data, kind 30078): store metadesk app/config data and address-book/host metadata as replaceable app-data events, so settings and saved hosts follow the identity across devices.
- NIP-44: encrypt any private payloads (address book contents, per-host notes/credentials, app-data, non-public list entries) with NIP-44 before publishing to relays. Nothing sensitive leaves the device in cleartext.
- Keep the existing session-negotiation stack (NIP-44-encrypted DMs, NIP-17 where applicable) and signer abstractions (NIP-46/55L/5F) as the identity/signing backbone.

Design doc must map each UX feature to the Nostr primitive it uses (and justify any case where a non-Nostr/local mechanism is chosen instead), plus relay strategy (which relays, user-configurable, NIP-65 outbox considerations) and offline/first-run behavior when no relay is reachable.
notes:
2026-11-16 decision (user): metadesk supports a signer interface like Groundhog/GNostr and lets the user decide which key is used for what. Design: signer accounts (backend,pubkey,label) over MdSigner backends 55L/5F/46; user-assigned host + client role bindings (same account may fill both); FIPS hosting validates host-role key == FIPS node key; NIP-46 creds in Secret Service/Keychain (Groundhog GhNip46CredentialStore pattern) — persistent NIP-46 pairing now in scope; CLI binding for headless hosts. Mirrors Groundhog GhAccountController in plain-C core (src/core/accounts.c). New work item P2.7. See docs/plans/management-ux-2026-11-14.md §7.6.

Why: metadesk host/client has been exercised mostly on a single pairing (macOS client ↔ Ubuntu/GNOME VM host over direct IP). We need a documented, repeatable end-to-end test matrix that covers every supported platform as both host and client, over both transports, so regressions in capture, encode/decode, a11y, input injection, session negotiation, and FIPS routing are caught.

What: Define and run an E2E matrix.

- Transports: (a) direct IP (LAN/IPv6 over TUN-less path), (b) FIPS mesh (npub, NIP-44 session negotiation, TCP over FIPS TUN).
- Per-cell checks: connect/auth, video (frames flow, correct dims, fills window, no trails), decode/FPS/bitrate, overlay, HUMAN input (mouse move/button/scroll + keyboard, correct button mapping, 1:1 cursor mapping), AGENT path (MCP tools, a11y tree, action-by-id), reconnect/restore, clean teardown.
